Is the 'flipped line removed == manifest hash' drift check sound? YES for its stated guarantee: hidden_original() only recognizes two exact reconstructions (append of the exact INVISIBLE_LINE suffix, or single exact VISIBLE_LINE->INVISIBLE_LINE substitution) and requires sha256(reconstruction) == receipt hash. Any additional byte edit changes the reconstructed hash and fails the proof (test_a_flip_plus_any_other_edit_is_still_drift), and no other file content can be 'smuggled' as unchanged because the reconstruction space is exactly two candidates, not an open-ended undo.

Does apply() only touch kit-owned, unmodified files? YES -- kit = _kit_skill_hashes(manifest_hashes(root)) restricts to receipt-listed skills/*/SKILL.md; per-file it additionally requires sha(data)==expected (byte-identical) before flipping, else 'locally modified' skip; project-owned skills (absent from kit) are skipped with reason. Symlinks explicitly rejected via path.is_symlink() check before any read/write.

Does --restore fully reverse? YES for files apply() flipped: tree_digest byte-comparison test (test_restore_is_byte_identical...) is a real assertion the ops file's own test suite makes; restore iterates the same kit-hash set and writes back hidden_original() when present, via write_atomic. Restore does not filter by protected_skills (verified by reading apply()'s restore branch), which is correct/intentional: it also restores a hand-hidden protected skill, matching the stated converge behavior and test_a_hand_hidden_protected_skill_is_drift_and_apply_restores_it.

Path traversal from profile names? NO -- skills.NAME_RE = r'[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*' (fullmatch) rejects any entry with '.', '/', or other traversal characters before any per-name logic runs (validated for the WHOLE profile before any write, in the `if not restore` bad-name check).

Fail-closed on refusal? YES -- manifest missing, malformed profile, non-skill-id disabled entry, and any protected name in disabled all raise SkillFitError before the per-skill loop begins; tree_digest-equality tests confirm zero writes occur on each refusal path.
